# CadKit script API: guide for LLM agents

CadKit builds parametric solids from a short JavaScript script. Every call on the part chain adds ONE normal feature (sketch, extrude, cut, hole, fillet, pattern ...) to a history tree; the kernel regenerates it and returns exact numbers. You never write geometry kernel calls: you write `part('Name').sketch(...).extrude(...)`, run it with `run_script`, and then PROVE the result with `facts`, `bodies`, `probe`, `section(s)` and `snapshot`.

## Units and conventions

* Millimetres and degrees. Y is up. Right-handed axes.
* `circle(r)` takes a RADIUS, `hole()` and `holes.*` take a DIAMETER.
* A script builds ONE part: `part(name)` then a chain. Each extrude / cut / revolve CONSUMES the sketch just before it (sketch again for the next feature).
* `variables({ w: 60, t: 'w/10' })` declares named values (strings are expressions); `expr('w*2')` keeps a feature parameter linked to them.

## Sketch planes and their frames (this is where most mistakes happen)

| plane | sketch x (u) | sketch y (v) | normal | extrude goes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `'front'` | world +X | world +Y | +Z | +Z |
| `'top'` | world +X | world -Z | +Y | +Y |
| `'right'` | world -Z | world +Y | +X | +X |

So on 'top' a larger sketch y moves towards the BACK (world -Z); on 'right' a larger sketch x moves towards world -Z. `plane('top').toWorld([u, v], offset)` gives the world point.

* `at('front', 20)` is the plane moved 20 mm along its normal (top along +Y, right along +X); `at(face('>Z'), 5)` offsets a planar face along its outward normal.
* `sketch(face('>Z'), ...)`: the sketch origin is the world origin projected on that face; u/v follow the face's own frame. Hole centres are [u, v] in that frame.
* Any plane: `at({ origin: [x, y, z], normal: [nx, ny, nz], xdir: [dx, dy, dz] })` (or `part.workplane(...)` for a plane feature of its own). Frame: the sketch origin is `origin`; sketch x (u) = xdir projected perpendicular to the normal; sketch y (v) = normal x u. Example: normal [1,0,0], xdir [0,0,1] gives u = +Z, v = X x Z = -Y. GIVE xdir whenever the orientation matters. Without xdir an axis-aligned normal is the standard plane of that axis (frames above), an oblique normal gets u = normal x [1,0,0].
* A tilt about a world axis: `at('front', 10, { rotate: { axis: 'x', angle: 30 } })`.

## Extrude, cut, revolve, sweep

* `extrude(d)` goes ALONG the sketch normal; `direction: 'into' | 'away' | 'both'`, `mid: true` (symmetric, d is the total), `draft`, `thin`. A sketch on a face adds material outward (a boss).
* `cut(d)` / `cut(through())` removes material. Default direction 'auto': it tries against the sketch normal (into the body from a face sketch) and flips once if the kernel says cutNoEffect (the run then carries the warning 'cut direction flipped automatically'). Say `direction: 'into' | 'away' | 'both'` to skip the retry.
* A cut applies to EVERY body that exists when it runs. A through-cut for the base plate's holes also slits an earlier body that crosses it. Build later parts after the cut, or leave clearance. The run warns when one cut changed several bodies.
* `revolve(360)`: the sketch must be the HALF profile on one side of the axis (x = distance from the axis, y = height; the axis is the sketch y axis unless `axis: { from, to }`). Drawing both sides gives profileCrossesAxis.
* `sweep(profile, path)`: both are `{ on, draw }` objects; the profile plane must be perpendicular to the path where the path starts; paths are planar sketches (a vertical plane per path for 3D routings). The path can be a helix: `p.helix({ radius, pitch, revolutions }); const h = p.handle(); p.sweep(profile, { curve: h })`. `guides: [{ on, draw }]` (one or two sketches, each ONE curve touching the profile and running along the path) with `guideMode: 'scale' | 'turn' | 'stretch'` makes the section follow the guides (a flare, a taper); no `twist` with guides.
* Two solids that touch or overlap FUSE into one body. Keep them apart with `newBody`: `extrude(10, { newBody: true })` or `{ newBody: 'Magnet' }` (also revolve and sweep, never for a cut). Use `bodies` to confirm the body count; a clearance of 0.1 mm also keeps parts separate.

## Direct edits and body operations

* `draft(faces, angle, { neutral })` tapers walls about a neutral plane ('front' | 'top' | 'right', `at(...)`, `face(...)`; its normal is the pull direction, `flip` reverses). `moveFace(faces, { distance })` pushes or pulls faces along their normals; `{ translate: [x, y, z] }` moves planar faces.
* `lip(rim, edges, { width, height })` raises a band on a planar rim; `groove(...)` cuts the same band into a rim (a lid). `rim` is `face(...)`, `edges` the rim edges (`edges({ onFace: rim })` also picks the inner rim edges of a shell: exclude them with `not`).
* Bodies: `scale(factor | [sx, sy, sz], { about: 'origin' | 'centroid', at, bodies })`; `moveBody(bodies, { translate, rotate: { axis, origin, angle }, copy, body, mirror })` (rotation first, then translation; bodies are not united afterwards); `split(target, tools)` cuts a body into the part outside and the part inside the tool bodies; `deleteBody(bodies, { keep })` takes names, handles or `face(...)`. Bodies are named with `newBody: 'Name'`.
* `deleteFace(faces)` turns the solid into a sheet without those faces. It does NOT heal the gap (the kernel has no heal mode yet); use it to open a shell for surface work, not to remove a hole.
* `sphere(radius, { centre, op, newBody })` needs no sketch. `helix({ radius, pitch | height | revolutions (two of them), on })` adds a curve only. `axis('y')` / `axis(edges(...))` / `axis(face(cylinder))` / `axis(planeA, planeB)` adds a reference axis feature (take its `handle()`). `dome` is not built in the kernel; do not try it through `feature()`.

* Parts from the wizards are their own bodies, placed by `origin` and `axis`: `nut({ size: 'M5', type })`, `standoff({ size, length, kind, ends })`, `heatSetInsert({ size, hole })`, `spring({ outer, wire, length, coils, ends: 'ground' })`, `extensionSpring(...)`, `torsionSpring(...)`, `caseBox({ width, depth, height, lidHeight })` (a closed two-part case, stands up from `origin`), plus `screw`, `washer` and `bearing`. `docs({ names })` lists the options of each.

## Handles, bodies, names, appearance

* `const h = part.handle()` right AFTER a feature returns a handle on that feature. Use it in `face('>Z', { of: h })`, `faces({ createdBy: h })`, patterns (`linearPattern(h, ...)`, `circularPattern([h1, h2], ...)`: the seed may be 'last', a handle, an id like 'F7', or an ARRAY), `appearance` and `bodyName`.
* A body (a connected lump) is identified by the feature that created it. `bodyName(h, 'Rotor')` names it (a pattern's bodies are numbered 'Rotor 1', 'Rotor 2').
* `appearance({ feature: h, colour: '#b87333', opacity: 0.2, finish: 'plastic' })` styles the bodies a feature created. finish is 'matte' | 'plastic' | 'chrome' | 'glass' | 'brushed'; 'brushed' and 'chrome' are metallic and make colours read grey, so use 'plastic' or 'matte' for coloured parts. A pattern's appearance also covers the seed's body. `{ face: 'F3.C1' }` / `{ face: 'F3.*' }` / `{ face: handle }` styles single faces. Appearance is view state (no geometry, no undo step); a .ckpart keeps it and STEP does not.
* `group('Name', () => { ... })` (or `part.group`) puts the features it records in a named folder of the tree.
* `insertPart(doc, { at, fixed, name })` inserts another part's document as a component; `mate(...)` positions it.

## Holes

Use hole FEATURES (`hole`, `holes.points`, `holes.polar`, `holes.grid`) for anything that should be a hole: the drawing layer lists callouts such as "M2.5 TAPPED DEPTH 2" only for real hole features, not for a sketch circle plus a cut.

## Workflow

1. `list_methods { query }` / `docs { names }`: read the exact signatures of what you use. Do not guess option names.
2. `run_script { mode: 'new', code }`. It is atomic: an error leaves the document unchanged and names the line (and the kernel code with a repair hint).
3. Check: `facts` (volume, bbox, solids, validity; pass `expect` for pass/fail checks), `bodies` (one row per body: name, creating feature, volume, bbox, colour), `probe` (is there material at a point), `section` / `sections` (exact slices), `tree`. Numeric design questions have their own read-only tools: `measure { a, b }` (distance and closest points between bodies, faces, edges, points), `clearance { required }` (gap between two bodies, pass or fail), `interference` (do bodies overlap, by how many mm3; a part that must stay separate needs `newBody`), `thickness { min }` (thinnest wall and where), `draft { pull, min }` (draft angle per face against a pull direction) and `dfm { process: 'injection' | 'cnc' | 'printing' }` (design-for-manufacture issues per rule, with faces and numbers). Bodies are named as `bodies` lists them; each result gives a verdict, so use them to check your own work instead of estimating.
4. Look: `snapshot { view: 'iso' | 'front' | 'top' | ... }`; with `section` for an internal view, `sheet` for a multi-view sheet. For a real engineering drawing (dimensions, hole callouts, sections, PDF/SVG/DXF) use `drawing`.
5. `checkpoint` before a risky change, `undo` / `restore` after. Use `mode: 'attach'` to ADD to what the user has built by hand (their features are kept).
6. Export with `export { format: 'step' | 'stl' | 'glb' | 'ckpart', path }`. For a `.ckpart` that opens at once in the app, add `cache: true`: the built view is stored in the file (refused with `view_unavailable` for a part with a curated or embedded font (text in the built-in fonts is fine), or a rolled-back part).

## Sheet metal

Sheet metal parts are ordinary script features: sheetRules (stock), baseFlange or contourFlange (first plate) or sheetConvert (from a solid), edgeFlange, hem, fold, sheetCut, sheetCorner, then unfold / refold. The flat pattern, bend table and DXF are results of those features, read with sheet_info and sheet_export. sheet_reference { feature } documents each feature with defaults and units. A sheet feature error carries the kernel code (flangeHeightTooLow, invalidValue with a field, sheetMetalUnsupported, nothingToCut) and a repair hint.

Sheet metal recipe: rules -> base flange -> flanges / hems -> flat pattern -> DXF

1. run_script: define the stock, draw ONE closed outline, make the base flange, then flange the edges.
   Edges are picked by a WORLD point on them (rect(100, 60) on 'front' is centred on the origin: edges at x = +-50, y = +-30; z = the thickness is the cap face, z = 0 the front face).

   part('Tray')
     .sheetRules({ name: 'Steel2', thickness: 2, kFactor: 0.44, bendRadius: 2 })
     .sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(100, 60))
     .baseFlange({ rule: 'Steel2' })
     .edgeFlange([[0, -30, 2], [0, 30, 2], [-50, 0, 2], [50, 0, 2]], { height: 15 });

2. sheet_info: the rule, the flat pattern after the last sheet feature (flatSize = width, length, thickness; bends with direction, angle, radius, allowance, line; bend zones) and advice on the rule. Tray above: flat 123.0478 x 83.0478 x 2, four 90 degree bends of allowance 4.5239 each.
3. facts / bodies: the folded solid (bodies lists the sheet metal summary on the base body).
4. sheet_export { format: 'dxf', path } writes the flat pattern DXF (layers CUT_OUTER, CUT_INNER, BEND_UP, BEND_DOWN; bendNotes, tangentLines, units, version options); { format: 'csv' | 'json' } returns the bend table.
5. Part of an edge, shaped legs: edgeFlange (and hem, for the first three) take start / length (mm along the picked edge from its start vertex, the outline runs counter-clockwise) or from / to (two world points on the edge, any order), relief ('none' | 'rectangular' | { width, depth }, the notch beside a partial flange), profile (the leg outline: 'sketch' = the last sketch, or { sketch: id }, or an inline loop of { line } / { arc } in the flange's own frame: v along the flange from the start of the span, h outward from the height line; circles inside a sketch outline are holes, inline holes go in holes: [{ circle: { center: [v, h], radius } }]):

   .edgeFlange([[50, 0, 2]], { height: 20, start: 20, length: 40, relief: 'rectangular' })      // 40 mm of the edge
   .sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(40, 20)).edgeFlange([[50, 0, 2]], { profile: 'sketch', from: [20, 0, 1], to: [60, 0, 1] })   // leg from a sketch (x = v, y = h)

6. Optional: add .unfold() to turn the body into the flat sheet (refold() undoes it), or .hem(...) for a 180 degree edge.

Rules of thumb
* Flat length = sum of the legs and flats + one bend allowance per bend, BA = (radius + kFactor x thickness) x angle (radians).
* heightFrom 'outer' (default) measures a flange height to the outer virtual sharp: leg = height - (radius + thickness) x tan(angle / 2). The height must reach the end of the bend (flangeHeightTooLow).
* A flange may cover part of an edge (start / length or from / to); the edge is then split in pieces and a later pick names the piece it is nearest to, so give later flanges from / to. A span must lie inside one free piece of the edge. With a profile the height is the top of the outline (leave height out), the outline must reach down to the bend line (the part below the end of the bend is the bend), and from / to must run along the edge's direction (counter-clockwise outline) or the outline comes out mirrored and fails with 'the profile does not reach beyond the bend': swap from and to and mirror it. A hole is listed once: a sketch's own inner loops already are holes. A hem takes start / from / to and relief, not length (its length is the hem's size).
* One flange per edge. Folds, flanges and hems combine in any order (panel tree); pick a flange edge on a leg with 'P2.tip' or { edge, panel }. Holes and slots go in with sheetCut (sketch in the flat layout, works across bends); a plain cut or hole breaks the sheet. Corners: sheetCorner round / chamfer; reliefs: cornerReliefShape notch | round | rectangular | tear on the rule. A solid bent plate becomes a sheet with sheetConvert.
* Keep bendRadius >= thickness and reliefWidth >= thickness: smaller values build, but crack in real stock (sheet_info reports them as advice).
* Picks by role ({ role: 'P0.side.e2' }) follow the sketch curve when the outline changes; points do not.

Limits (not in the kernel yet, do not script them): flanges on curved edges (a base outline with arcs takes flanges on its straight edges), relief shapes other than a rectangle for partial flanges, arcs or several chains in a contour flange, a zig-zag fold chain on a concave base, sheetCorner across bends, sheetConvert of cones, tori or free-form bends, sheetCut that splits a panel. sheet_reference lists the status of every feature.

## Worked example: a bracket with a rib

```js
part('Clevis')
  .sketch('top', (s) => s.rrect(140, 90, 8)).extrude(12)
  .holes.points(face('>Y'), [[-55, -30], [55, -30], [-55, 30], [55, 30]], { diameter: 10 })
  .sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(30, 79, [15, 45.5])).extrude(60, { mid: true })   // block
  .sketch('front', (s) => s.circle(25, [15, 85])).extrude(60, { mid: true })       // boss
  .sketch('front', (s) => s.line([-50, 12], [-5, 70])).rib(15)                     // rib: ONE open line
  .sketch('front', (s) => s.circle(15, [15, 85])).cut(through(), { direction: 'both' }); // bore
```

Volume 335157 mm3, one valid body. The rib is ONE open line, centred on the sketch plane, 15 total thickness, extended past both ends until it meets the body and fused. The web stops at the outer wall of the body and never fills a bore, so the rib may come before or after the bore. Options: `.rib(15, { fillet: 3, draft: 2, side: 'right', target: 'Bracket' })` rounds the free edge (radius below half the thickness), tapers the two sides (degrees, one straight line only), puts all the thickness on one side of the sketch plane ('left' | 'right', default 'both') and grows to the named body only. Gotchas: a through cut from a sketch on the mid-plane needs `direction: 'both'` (the run warns when it is left out); a closed triangle in rib gives ribNeedsOpenSketch, and extruding one open line gives noClosedProfile (use `rib` for a web, `thin` for a thin wall).

## Worked example: a two-part case

```js
part('Case')
  .sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(80, 50)).extrude(30)
  .feature({ type: 'shell', faces: [], thickness: 2 })                  // no open face: a closed cavity
  .lipJoint(at('front', 15), { height: 1.5, width: 1, clearance: 0.2, names: ['Base', 'Lid'] });
```

Two valid bodies, Base (14930 mm3) and Lid (13952.24 mm3); total 29104 + 378 - 599.76 = 28882.24 (box + tongue - groove). The tongue is 1 mm wide and 1.5 mm high, centred in the 2 mm wall; the groove is 0.2 mm wider on each side and 0.2 mm deeper. `split(plane, { names })` alone cuts a body into two named bodies. A mould is: `scale` the part body by 1/(1-shrinkage), a block as `newBody`, `combine('cut', block, part, { keepTools: true })`, then `split(plane, { target: block })`. Not yet: draft, a curved or stepped parting surface, undercut detection.

## Common errors and what to do

| code | meaning | fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cutNoEffect | the cut tool does not overlap the material | check the plane frame (table above) and the sketch coordinates; use `direction`; a sketch circle outside the body misses in BOTH directions |
| nothingToCut | a cut ran with no body yet | build the base solid first |
| profileCrossesAxis | revolve profile lies on both sides of the axis | draw half of the profile, from the axis outwards |
| sweepProfileNotNormal | profile plane is not perpendicular to the path start | sketch the profile on the plane the path leaves at right angles |
| booleanFailed | the union / cut could not be completed | move the tool by 0.01 mm, avoid coincident faces, unite touching bodies first |
| unsupported selector / Line N | a face()/edges() selector found nothing | selectors resolve against the body just before that step; print `tree` and use `find` for names |
| unknown method | not in the API | `list_methods { query }` |
| flangeHeightTooLow | a sheet flange is shorter than its bend | raise the height (the error gives minHeight) or reduce radius / angle |
| invalidValue (field) | a sheet feature value or pick is wrong | the hint names the field; edges are world points on the base outline |
| sheetMetalUnsupported | a sheet case the kernel does not build yet | the hint says what to reorder (flange before cuts, fold before flanges) |

## Performance

A part with many hundred features regenerates in seconds. Patterns of bodies are the heavy part; prefer one `hole` feature with many points (`holes.polar`) over a loop of `hole()` calls.

## Method index

Call forms: `part.m()` chains on the part, `s.m()` on the sketch builder `s`, the rest are plain functions. Ask `docs { names: [...] }` for parameters, notes and an example.

### sketch

* `at(base, offset?, opts?)`: A workplane for a sketch: an offset plane, a face, a plane feature, a point and normal, or a tilt.
* `.sketch(plane, build, name?)`: Start a sketch on a plane or a face; the next extrude, cut or revolve uses it.
* `.sketchFeature(on, json)`: Append a raw sketch (points, entities, constraints) on a plane.
* `.workplane(base, offset?, opts?)`: /** Add a reference plane (workplane) feature without a sketch.
* `plane(name)`: The frame of a standard sketch plane: which world axes its sketch x, y and normal are.
* `s.arc(centre, start, end)`: Counter-clockwise arc about a centre from a start point to an end point.
* `s.arc3(a, m, b)`: Arc from a to b passing through the middle point m (either direction).
* `s.axis()`: Construction line along the sketch Y axis (the default revolve axis).
* `s.axisAt(from, to)`: Construction line used as the revolve axis when it is not the sketch Y axis.
* `s.circle(r, at?)`: Circle given its RADIUS (not diameter).
* `s.curve(f, o?)`: Curve from a JavaScript function t -> [x, y], sampled into a fitted spline.
* `s.cvspline(pts, o?)`: Control-vertex spline: the points are the control polygon, not on the curve.
* `s.equation(o)`: Curve from formulas x(t), y(t): the kernel fits a spline with the fewest points within the tolerance.
* `s.grid(origin, pitch, count)`: Points on a rectangular grid.
* `s.line(a, b)`: One line segment between two points.
* `s.offset(distance, o?)`: Offset the chain drawn last.
* `s.point(at)`: A single point (a hole centre).
* `s.points(pts)`: Several points (hole centres).
* `s.polar(count, draw?, o?)`: Repeat a drawing around a centre.
* `s.polarCurve(f, o?)`: Polar curve from a function angle -> radius (waves, cams, petals).
* `s.polarPoints(center, radius, n, startAngle?)`: Points on a circle: a bolt circle of centres.
* `s.polygon(pts)`: Closed polygon through the points.
* `s.polyline(pts)`: Open chain of lines through the points.
* `s.rect(w, h, at?)`: Rectangle of width x height centred on a point.
* `s.rrect(w, h, r, at?)`: Rounded rectangle: width x height with corner radius r.
* `s.spline(pts, o?)`: Interpolating spline: a smooth curve through the points.
* `s.text(string, at, opts?)`: Lettering: the outlines of a string as closed regions (engrave it with cut, emboss it with extrude).

### features

* `bearing(o)`: A ball bearing as separate bodies (rings, balls when open), placed by an origin and an axis.
* `caseBox(o)`: A closed two-part case (Base and Lid with a lip joint) in one call.
* `extensionSpring(o)`: An extension spring as its own body.
* `heatSetInsert(o)`: A heat-set insert as its own body, optionally with its hole.
* `nut(o)`: A hexagon nut as its own body.
* `.axis(a, b?)`: A reference axis: a world axis, a straight edge, a cylinder or the line where two planes meet.
* `.baseFlange(o?)`: Sheet base plate from the last closed sketch.
* `.bearing(o)`: A ball bearing as separate bodies: two rings (with shields or seals) and, when open, the balls.
* `.caseBox(o)`: A closed two-part case (base and lid with a lip joint) from outside sizes.
* `.chamfer(on, distance)`: Bevel edges: equal distance, two distances, or distance and angle.
* `.combine(op, target, tools, o?)`: Boolean between whole bodies: union, cut, intersect or split.
* `.contourFlange(o)`: Sheet base from an open chain of sketch lines.
* `.cut(end, o?)`: Cut the last sketch out of the body: a depth or through().
* `.deleteBody(bodies, o?)`: Remove whole bodies, or keep only some.
* `.deleteFace(faces)`: Delete faces: the solid becomes an open sheet without them.
* `.draft(faces, angle, o)`: Draft (taper) faces about a neutral plane.
* `.edgeFlange(edges, o)`: Bent flange on edges of the base plate.
* `.extensionSpring(o)`: An extension spring as its own body.
* `.extrude(depth, o?)`: Extrude the last sketch into a solid (adds material).
* `.feature(json)`: Append any kernel feature as raw JSON (escape hatch for features without a helper).
* `.fillet(on, radius)`: Round edges: one radius, a radius per edge, or a variable radius.
* `.fold(o)`: Fold the base along a line.
* `.gear(o)`: Involute spur or helical gear (profile, body extrude, bore) from module and teeth.
* `.groove(rim, edges, o?)`: Groove along rim edges (the mating half of a lip).
* `.heatSetInsert(o)`: A heat-set threaded insert as its own body, optionally with its hole.
* `.helix(o)`: A helix curve (adds no body): the path of a sweep, or a reference.
* `.hem(edges, o)`: 180 degree hem on an edge.
* `.knurl(o)`: Knurl a cylinder: cut straight, diamond or pyramid grooves into it.
* `.lip(rim, edges, o?)`: Raise a lip: a band along rim edges (a rabbet for a lid).
* `.lipJoint(plane, o)`: Lip joint of a two-part case: split a shelled body at a plane, tongue on one half, groove on the other.
* `.loft(sections, o?)`: Loft a solid through two or more section sketches, optionally ending in a point.
* `.moveBody(bodies, o?)`: Move, rotate or copy whole bodies (also a mirrored copy).
* `.moveFace(faces, o)`: Push or pull faces; their neighbours follow (direct modelling).
* `.nut(o)`: A hexagon nut (ISO 4032, 4035, 4033) as its own body.
* `.refold()`: Refold an unfolded sheet.
* `.revolve(angle?, o?)`: Revolve the last sketch about an axis (lathe parts: pulleys, bushings, flanges).
* `.rib(thickness, o?)`: Rib: a web of a given thickness from an open sketch line, grown to the body.
* `.scale(factor, o?)`: Scale bodies uniformly or per axis (print shrink compensation, stretched variants).
* `.screw(o)`: A screw or bolt as its own body: head, drive and shank, placed by an origin and an axis.
* `.sheetConvert(o?)`: Turn a bent-plate solid into a sheet metal part.
* `.sheetCorner(corners, o?)`: Round or chamfer free convex corners of the sheet.
* `.sheetCut(o?)`: Cut closed sketch regions out of the sheet, across bends too.
* `.sheetRules(o?)`: Sheet stock rule: thickness, k-factor, bend radius.
* `.shell(open, thickness)`: Hollow the body to a wall thickness, opening the selected face(s).
* `.sphere(radius, o?)`: A ball, without a sketch.
* `.split(target, tools?, o?)`: Split a body in two: with tool bodies, or at a plane.
* `.spring(o)`: A compression spring as its own body.
* `.standoff(o)`: A round or hex standoff, female-female or male-female, as its own body.
* `.sweep(profile, path, o?)`: Sweep a closed profile along a path sketch (pipes, rails, handles).
* `.thin(thickness)`: Make the previous extrude or revolve a thin-walled one.
* `.thread(on, o)`: Add a cosmetic or modeled screw thread to a bore or cylinder.
* `.torsionSpring(o)`: A torsion spring as its own body.
* `.unfold()`: Unfold the sheet to its flat body.
* `.washer(o)`: A flat or split spring washer as its own body, placed by an origin and an axis.
* `screw(o)`: A screw or bolt as its own body (head, drive, shank), placed by an origin and an axis.
* `spring(o)`: A compression spring as its own body.
* `standoff(o)`: A standoff as its own body.
* `through()`: End condition for cut(): through all material.
* `torsionSpring(o)`: A torsion spring as its own body.
* `washer(o)`: A flat or split spring washer as its own body, placed by an origin and an axis.

### selectors

* `edges(sel)`: Select edges of the current body by direction, extreme plane, or a rule object.
* `face(sel, opts?)`: Select ONE face of the current body: by direction, by persistent name, by feature, or by a rule.
* `faces(sel, opts?)`: Select SEVERAL faces (a set) of the current body, or choose one of them by order, size or position.

### holes

* `.hole(on, at, o)`: A simple drilled hole on a planar face at [x, y].
* `.holes.grid(on, g, o)`: A rectangular grid of holes.
* `.holes.points(on, pts, o)`: Drill holes at listed coordinates: one hole feature at a list of centres.
* `.holes.polar(on, c, o)`: A bolt circle: drill a polar array of count holes equally spaced on a circle.

### patterns

* `.circularPattern(seed, o?)`: Repeat features around an axis.
* `.linearPattern(seed, o?)`: Repeat features along a direction, optionally as a 2D grid.
* `.mirror(plane, o?)`: Mirror the last feature (or the whole body) about a plane.
* `.pathPattern(seed, o?)`: Repeat features along a path sketch, moved or turned with it.

### surfaces

* `.knit(o?)`: Surface: sew all surfaces so far into one body (a solid when they close).
* `.surfaceExtrude(depth, o?)`: Surface: extrude the last sketch into a sheet (no end caps, not a solid).
* `.surfaceLoft(sections)`: Surface: loft a sheet through section sketches (open or closed curves).
* `.surfacePlanar()`: Surface: a flat sheet filling the last closed sketch.
* `.thicken(thickness, o?)`: Surface: give the last surface a wall thickness and make it a solid.

### assembly

* `.insertPart(doc, o?)`: Assembly: insert another part (its document) as a component, optionally moved.
* `.mate(o)`: Assembly: constrain two faces of different components.

### utilities

* `expr(text)`: A parameter written as an expression over the variables.
* `group(name, build)`: Put the features recorded inside `build` in a named folder of the feature tree.
* `part(name?)`: Start a new part: the part the script builds; returns the fluent builder.
* `.appearance(o)`: Colour, opacity and finish of the bodies a feature made (view only, no geometry change).
* `.area()`: Read the total surface area (mm2) of the part built so far.
* `.bbox()`: Read the bounding box of the part built so far.
* `.bodyName(target, name)`: Name the bodies a feature made (shown in the Bodies list; the default is Body 1, 2, ...).
* `.centreOfMass()`: Read the centre of mass of the part built so far.
* `.edgeCount()`: Read the number of edges of the part built so far.
* `.edges()`: Read the edges of the part built so far: key, midpoint, length, adjacent faces.
* `.expectBBox(box, o?)`: Check the bounding box of the part built so far.
* `.expectFaceCount(n)`: Check the number of faces of the part built so far.
* `.expectMinFaceArea(a, o?)`: Check that no face of the part is smaller than a given area (no slivers).
* `.expectValid()`: Check that the part built so far passes the kernel's validity check.
* `.expectVolume(v, o?)`: Check the volume of the part built so far; a mismatch is reported as an error with this line.
* `.faceCount()`: Read the number of faces of the part built so far.
* `.faces()`: Read the faces of the part built so far: persistent name, kind, area, normal, centre, radius, feature.
* `.group(name, build)`: Put the features recorded inside `build` in a named folder of the feature tree.
* `.handle(label?)`: A handle on the feature recorded last, for face({ of }) and patterns.
* `.inertia(density?)`: Read the mass, first moments, inertia tensor and principal axes of the part built so far.
* `.issues()`: Read the validator's issues for the part built so far.
* `.isValid()`: Read whether the part built so far passes the kernel's validity check.
* `.textMetrics(string, opts?)`: Measure a string before drawing it: width, ink box and per-letter advances.
* `.upAxis(axis)`: Z-up or Y-up view hint.
* `.volume()`: Read the volume (mm3) of the part built so far.
* `variables(defs)`: Declare named values; strings are expressions over earlier ones.

## Recipes (complete scripts, `docs { names: [id] }` returns the code)

* `engraved-nameplate`: Nameplate with engraved lettering (text sized from its metrics)
* `two-part-case`: Two-part case: a hollow box split into base and lid with a tongue-and-groove joint
* `mould-from-part`: Mould halves from a part: shrink, block, cavity (keep the part), split
* `dial-numerals`: Dial with upright numerals on a 270 degree sweep and a caption on an arc
* `boss-by-feature-verified`: Plate with a boss: pick faces by feature and verify with read-backs
* `flanged-bushing`: Flanged bushing (revolved profile)
* `bolt-circle-plate`: Round plate with a centre bore and a bolt circle
* `l-bracket`: L-bracket with filleted corners and mounting holes
* `hollow-box-lid`: Hollow box: shell the walls, then close it with a lid
* `box-lip-groove`: Box with a lip on the rim (and the matching groove for the lid)
* `drafted-block`: Draft a wall for moulding
* `helix-coil`: A coil of wire: helix curve and a sweep along it
* `guided-sweep-frustum`: A sweep that flares along a guide curve
* `pulley`: Pulley: revolved groove profile plus lightening holes
* `spur-gear-blank`: Spur gear blank: disc, hub, bore and keyway (no teeth)
* `rib-plate`: Plate reinforced with ribs (ribs as thin extrudes)
* `tapered-boss-chamfer`: Tapered boss on a plate with a chamfered top edge
* `pocket-grid`: Grid of rectangular pockets in one feature
* `boat-hull-loft`: Boat hull: loft through four spline stations to a point bow
* `swept-pipe`: Swept pipe along an arc path
* `counterbored-plate`: Plate with a centre bore and four counterbored screw holes
* `mirrored-bracket`: Channel bracket: build half, mirror the body
* `verification`: How to verify a part (numbers first, then eyes)
* `sheet-metal-tray`: Sheet metal tray: rules, base flange, four flanges, flat pattern, DXF
* `common-errors`: Common errors and what to do about them
